solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Just light entertainment

definitions.meaning: light hair or skin is pale, blonde in colouring
a funfair or fairground is a travelling entertainment of rides and stalls

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that something is merely light entertainment, nothing weightier.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings of one word are packed in: 'Just', 'light' and 'entertainment' each define it on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means even-handed, pale-complexioned, and a funfair, so each of the three clue words is a synonym.

clue.text: Evidence of authority to issue weapons to troop

parts.note: to arm a force is to issue weapons to it
a troop is a group or company, a band

explanation.surface: Someone claims they have official authority to hand out weapons to a troop of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth band worn on the sleeve often marks an official, a steward or captain, showing their authority.

clue.text: Start to recover from exchange of shots

definitions.meaning: markets or patients ... when they begin to pick up again
in tennis a long exchange of strokes between players is a ...

explanation.surface: Someone begins to recuperate after a gunfight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange of shots' suggests gunfire, but here the shots are tennis strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rally means both a recovery and a prolonged series of strokes back and forth in racket sports.

clue.text: No confidence water vapour leads to corrosion

indicators.note: one piece leads to, i.e. comes before, the other in the answer

parts.note: mist is fine water vapour hanging in the air
rust is the corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: A grim scientific note: damp air causes metal to corrode, so the structure inspires no confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspicion or doubt is a lack of trust, which is the absence of confidence.

clue.text: Host accepts a coat

indicators.note: accepts means the first piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: MC, master of ceremonies, is the host of an event

explanation.surface: A party host takes a guest's coat at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: A MAC is a mackintosh, a British word for a waterproof raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh is a rubberised raincoat, so it is a kind of coat.

clue.text: Latest lie concocted that goes all round the world

definitions.text: that goes all round the world

indicators.note: something concocted is made up, cooked up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: The newest invented falsehood spreads globally, as lies tend to.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbiting spacecraft or moon circles the Earth, travelling round the whole globe.

clue.text: Go berserk, having to manage tumultuous crowd

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a riot is a violent disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A security officer loses it when told to control a rowdy mob.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to behave wildly and without restraint, just as going berserk does.

clue.text: Take boat round north, a slow mover

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the other

parts.note: to sail is to travel by boat

explanation.surface: A leisurely boat trip heading north, in a vessel that barely moves.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden mollusc is proverbial for its sluggish pace, so it is a slow mover.

clue.text: To be inferred, simplicity has no limits

indicators.note: losing its limits means the word drops its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A remark that simplicity, it is to be understood, is boundless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implied rather than stated outright has to be inferred by the listener.

clue.text: Cattle without water

definitions.meaning: an old word for cattle, oxen
a ... spirit is served undiluted, with no water or mixer

explanation.surface: A drought image: livestock with nothing to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat for cattle is archaic but a crossword favourite, as in neatsfoot oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an archaic term for bovine animals and also describes an undiluted drink.

clue.text: Cautious course across river

indicators.note: across means the first piece spans the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a way is a route or course

explanation.surface: Someone takes a careful route over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wary means being careful and on guard against danger.

clue.text: Liable to error, bail fell out!

indicators.note: out signals the letters are disordered, put out of place

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire's wry verdict: the bail fell, so somebody is out, mistakes happen.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bails sit on the stumps; one falling means the batsman is out, which hides 'out' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who can make mistakes is imperfect and capable of being wrong.

clue.text: Produce cabaret, if in resort

indicators.note: to resort is to sort again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion to stage a cabaret show if staying at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but reads as re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To fabricate is to make or construct, the same as producing something.

clue.text: Film villain is curious Old Testament character

parts.note: curious means strange or odd
Job is the long-suffering hero of the Old Testament book named after him

explanation.surface: A movie bad guy is said to be a strange biblical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddjob is the hat-throwing henchman in the James Bond film Goldfinger.

clue.text: Out of work, Jack has nothing to be thankful for

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
O, the figure zero, means nothing
to bless something is to be thankful for it, as in blessing one's luck

explanation.surface: Jack has lost his job and has nothing to be grateful for.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unemployed has no job, so is out of work.

clue.text: Perfect in diplomacy

parts.note: tact is sensitivity and diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: Praise for someone flawless in their handling of delicate affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whole and undamaged is complete and unbroken, so perfect in that sense.

clue.text: Hide in attic, once alone

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the following words, across their breaks

explanation.surface: A child hides up in the attic, once left alone in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal something is to keep it out of sight, to hide it.

clue.text: Irritable person, sensible, not coming forward

parts.note: a crab, short for crabby person, is a grumpy or irritable person
wise means sensible and judicious

explanation.surface: A grumpy but sensible person is reluctant to step forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving sideways like a crustacean means advancing obliquely rather than straight ahead.

clue.text: Argumentative sportsman?

parts.note: a sculler or oarsman pulls an oar, and the same spelling, rhyming with cow, suggests someone who quarrels

explanation.surface: A query about an athlete who picks fights.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for an oarsman is spelt the same as one who rows (rhymes with cows), that is, argues.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower is a sportsman who propels a boat with oars; read another way, one who quarrels.

clue.text: Naughty girl in furs, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound, not spelling

parts.note: minks are furs, coats made from the pelts of the mink

explanation.surface: A mischievous young woman swathed in expensive fur coats, so rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is a cheeky, flirtatious or impudent girl.

clue.text: Hyperactive person in charge

parts.note: man is a general word for a person

explanation.surface: A jittery, overexcited individual has been put in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic describes frenzied, overexcited energy, so it suits hyperactive.

clue.text: Insipidly sweet short message broken off

indicators.note: broken off means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a tweet is a short message posted on Twitter, now X

explanation.surface: A sickly-cute text that got cut off mid-sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee describes something affectedly dainty or cutesy, sweet to the point of being cloying.

clue.text: One's missing, having been east on tour

indicators.note: on tour suggests the letters are travelling about, moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is unaccounted for because they have been travelling in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is a person who is not present, someone missing from where they should be.

clue.text: Fixed a number of games

definitions.meaning: ... means fixed or established, as in a ... time
in tennis a ... is a group of games

explanation.surface: A match-fixing accusation: several games were rigged.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means firmly fixed and also a tennis unit made of several games.

clue.text: New Moon Street

definitions.meaning: the thin curved sliver seen just after a new moon is this shape
in British addresses a curved row of houses is often called this, as a street name

explanation.surface: Reads as an address: a road named New Moon Street.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a thin curved lunar phase and also a curved residential road in Britain.

clue.text: Young player left in bed

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A young sportsman has been left lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a colt is an inexperienced junior player, by analogy with a young horse.
